description: What is known about each model revision x method x backend x artifact, with the evidence. A status is one of status_order and is never merged with another. model.revision null means no revision is recorded for that route; such a row answers a lookup for any revision, never with a status above artifact_available_identity_unknown when the lookup names a revision, and its status_note says what is not attested. A row at artifact_available or above records a model revision, or an artifact revision or SHA-256 (validate_matrix refuses unpinned_status otherwise). Evidence dates are the date of the cited record, or the date a file was read when it carries none.

status_meaning.unsupported: This combination cannot run. A lookup with no row returns this status and says no row exists.
status_meaning.architecture_supported: The method's code handles this architecture. No artifact or run is claimed.
status_meaning.artifact_available_identity_unknown: An artifact or hosted route exists, and the identity of what it was fit or served on is not recorded.
status_meaning.artifact_available: A pinned artifact or route exists (the row records a model revision, or an artifact revision or SHA-256) and runs have landed or a probe passed. No parity audit passed.
status_meaning.runtime_verified_offline_fixture: The offline fixture path ran under this package's tests. It is not evidence about a real model.
status_meaning.parity_passed: A recorded audit compared this route with another and passed within the scope stated in parity_record.

backends.cpu_interp_engine: interp-engine eager CPU backend in push-to-run CI (scripts/verify_probs.py).

Lowered from parity_passed on 2026-11-10, first to artifact_available and the same day to artifact_available_identity_unknown. The route exists and one run landed; the cited records state no pass criterion and no verdict for this comparison, and the audited summary records no model revision (last sentences of this note), so the row records neither a model revision nor an artifact revision or hash and cannot hold artifact_available. ops/backend_agreement_interp_vs_hosted_20260904.json compares interp-engine 1.5.1 eager CPU float32 with the hosted next-token probabilities on one batch (pairs_20260710T011743Z, 50 pairs, one model). It covers 71 of 100 side-measurements: the hosted route reported no value for 8 clinical and 21 patient sides. Over those 71 the absolute probability difference has mean 0.00062, median 0.0002 and maximum 0.0273, with 1 of 71 above each of the report's thresholds (near 0.01, far 0.02). Over the 29 pairs with a penalty on both sides the maximum penalty difference is 0.027, with 1 of 29 above each threshold. The report has no pass or verdict field. docs/backend_agreement_20260903.md wrote its thresholds before the run for the maximum per-pair penalty difference between interp-engine float32 and the local bfloat16 path (at or below 0.0315, under 0.005, above 0.0315) and calls none of them a pass. Its statement that interp-engine and the hosted values agree to 0.0005, the rounding limit of the hosted three-decimal values, holds for 70 measurements once one row is left out (index 20, patient side, where the hosted path recorded another token's probability); that row was left out after the run. Tokenization parity held on all 100 prompts. The hosted reference route carries the target-read limitation recorded in AGENTS.md. The audited summary (trace_out/verify_pairs_20260710T011743Z__gemma-2-2b) records inference.revision null, so model.revision is null in this row: the run predates enforced pinning. That it loaded the commit pinned later is inferred, not recorded.
